chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: 'Indeed, Allah sanctified Mecca on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and it is sacred until the Hour arises. It was not permissible for anyone before me, nor will it be permissible for anyone after me, and it was not permissible for me except for a moment of a day.'
ai.seo_question: What is the duration and nature of Mecca's sanctity according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the eternal sanctity (Haramiyyah) of Mecca, tracing its consecration back to the primordial creation of the heavens and earth, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the exclusivity of the Prophet's permission to fight there. It highlights the unique status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) who was granted a temporary license to enter and fight during the Conquest, distinguishing his era from the perpetual prohibition for all other prophets and generations. This narrative reinforces the theological continuity of Mecca's holiness while underscoring the specific historical context of the Fath Makkah event.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said on the day he<sup>saww</sup> conquered Makkah that: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sanctified Makkah the day He<sup>azwj</sup> Created the skies and the earth, and it is a Al-Harram up to the Establishment of the Hour. It was not unrestricted for anyone before me<sup>saww</sup>, and it will not be unrestricted for anyone after me<sup>saww</sup>, and it is not unrestricted for me<sup>saww</sup> except for ‘a time’ of ‘a day’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“He (the Imam) has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, on the day of liberation of Makkah said, ‘Allah made Makkah sacred (restricted) on the day He created the skies and earth and it remains sacred until the Hour of doom. It never was unsacred (unrestricted) for anyone before me, it will never be unsacred for anyone after me, and it is not unsacred (unrestricted) for me except for one hour during the day (to deal with the enemy).”’
